ok so here's the draft benchmark summary i just threw together for the kiteDB evaluation doc — curious what you think before i submit it to the team 🤔

"KiteDB achieves a 2.1x reduction in write amplification compared to RocksDB's leveled compaction under sustained 110k ops/sec (7.1 vs 14.8). This is primarily due to our tiered compaction scheduler which prioritizes overlapping SST ranges, reducing unnecessary I/O churn. Early microbenchmarks show consistent latency within p99 of 2.3ms under mixed read/write workloads."

honestly feels solid but i have this nagging feeling i'm missing something big... like what about CPU starvation during concurrent flushes? rocksDB hits that wall hard at scale and i'm not sure i addressed it yet.

I'll pull the evaluation doc and any related notes first so the review is grounded in what you actually measured, not just the paragraph. I'll also check whether CPU starvation / concurrent flushes already showed up in the results.
